decisions.quote: Our results show significant differences in coral bleaching, calcification, survivorship, and mortality since 1970 in three species of corals ( L. scutaria , M. capitata, P. damicornis ). These corals show higher calcification rates at a similar temperature increase in 2017 as compared to 1970. Calcification rates remained impaired under elevated temperatures across species; however, the reductions in 2017 were not as severe as those documented in 1970.
decisions.reason: Elevated temperature (~31.4 °C) continued to impair calcification across species and increase bleaching and mortality in M. capitata and P. damicornis as in 1970, but the authors explicitly contrast the 2017 results with the 1970 findings, reporting significantly delayed bleaching and mortality, much higher survivorship instead of complete mortality at 31 °C, and no significant heated-versus-ambient mortality or survivorship difference in L. scutaria.

expert_decision_not_adopted.quote: Irradiance has been documented to have a significant influence on coral growth, bleaching, and mortality ( Jokiel & Coles, 1977 ; Coles & Jokiel, 1978 ; Hoegh-Guldberg & Smith, 1989 ; Goenaga & Canals, 1990 ; Fitt & Warner, 1995 ; Brown et al., 1999 ; Jokiel, 2004 ). Our investigation of response across irradiance levels determined that irradiance plays a key role in the recovery of corals. Corals exposed to identical temperatures with a 50% reduction in irradiance had a 17% lower mortality rate than those at full light exposure. However, calcification rates did not differ across irradiance levels during either the stress or recovery periods.
expert_decision_not_adopted.reason: Addressing the prior scope objection regarding irradiance: Coles & Jokiel (1978, 'Synergistic effects of temperature, salinity and light on the hermatypic coral Montipora verrucosa') studied temperature, salinity, and light interactions in M. verrucosa alone, whereas the 2017 study did not manipulate salinity and did not compare its 50% shading manipulation against any 1970/1978 irradiance data. In the 2017 experiment, irradiance had no effect on calcification during the stress or recovery period (p = 0.442) and affected partial mortality only during the 28-day recovery period (p = 0.016), for which the authors note 'no recovery measurements were reported from 1970'. All 1970-versus-2017 empirical comparisons in Results (Figs. 4-6, Table 3) are restricted to ambient/full-sun irradiance across all three species from the 30-day experiment represented by Jokiel & Coles (1977) in shipped row 729, while Coles & Jokiel (1978) is cited in Results solely for historical tank temperature standard deviations (0.9-1.2 °C) and in Discussion as part of a seven-paper background list on irradiance.

(1975, 'Effects of thermal loading on Hawaiian reef corals', EPA Ecological Research Series technical report, 285 pp.) is not an independent original study but the comprehensive EPA technical report for the same 1970 Hawaiian coral thermal-loading experiment whose mortality and growth results were published in the peer-reviewed journal article Jokiel & Coles (1977) (shipped row 729). In Results, both the 30-day survivorship and ambient control data cited to Jokiel & Coles (1977) and the day-3 whole-colony mortality counts at 31 °C (n = 15, n = 8, n = 3 out of n = 20 per species) cited to Jokiel et al. (1975) describe and are plotted on the same 1970 survivorship curves in Figure 5 ('comparison of the Jokiel and Coles 1970 experiment with the current experiment').
